summary:
The ink module is done: children can answer by handwriting (pen or finger), physical keyboard or on-screen keypad. Typecheck shows 0 errors in src/ink (excluding src/ink/ml), 84 unit tests pass, and all 3 Playwright tests pass against the real model.

NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR ABOUT THE USER'S MESSAGE: the user asked in Spanish where the Supabase work is ("donde me has dejado lo de supabase no lo veo"). This module does not touch Supabase. What exists right now: docs/SUPABASE_SETUP.md (step-by-step setup guide), .env.example (VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY) and an EMPTY supabase/migrations/ folder. The guide tells the user to run supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql, but that file has not been written yet; it belongs to the data agent, and src/data/index.ts is still a stub. The user should be told this plainly.

How it works:
- Capture engine (capture.ts, InkCapture, no React): Pointer Events with setPointerCapture, getCoalescedEvents when available, coordinates that ignore the cell border. touch-action:none plus non-passive touchstart/touchmove preventDefault, and contextmenu/selectstart/dragstart blocked, so iPad Safari does not scroll, zoom, select text or show the callout. No <input> elements anywhere (avoids iPadOS Scribble); ink surfaces are focusable divs with role=textbox.
- A stroke only counts as started once it moves past the tap slop or lasts longer than a tap, so a quick tap never wipes a cell's state. If a pointer's pointerup is lost (same id comes down again, or it has been silent for 1.5 s), it is closed so it cannot block the next stroke.
- Palm rejection (policy.ts): penSeen is stored in localStorage under 'numeria.ink.penSeen'; only real (isTrusted) pen events set it. Once set, fingers on ink surfaces can only tap. A pen landing while a finger is writing drops the finger stroke as a palm. Extra: buttons next to the writing area (✓, eraser, keypad keys, toggles) ignore finger presses while the pen is touching the screen or within 300 ms after. Pen hover does not count, so a quick deliberate finger tap still works.
- Pen eraser: buttons bit 32, button 5, or the S Pen barrel button (bit 2).
- Drawing (render.ts): DPR-scaled canvas a little larger than the cell so ink can overflow; smooth quadratic curves through midpoints; deep-plum ink colour read from the CSS colour; pen pressure changes only the line width.
- DigitCell: recognises 620 ms after pen-up (gives time for the second stroke of 4, 5, 7). The result is typeset in Fredoka over ink faded to 16%, with a bounce-in animation. Confidence below 0.6 shows a small gold "?"; tapping it opens chips with the top 3 alternatives plus a "write again" pencil. When the recogniser returns no digit, tapping shows its alternatives (or all 0–9 if it has none). Picking a different digit counts as a recognition fix and stores a 'corrected' sample.
- Clearing a cell: scribble-out, pen eraser, a small clear button on the focused cell (56px hit area), or a quick pen tap on a recognised cell to rewrite it. A finger tap never erases once a pen has been used.
- Rewriting rules: a new stroke within 1.8 s, or a short stroke later (a 7's bar, a 5's hat), adds to the current digit; a tall stroke later replaces it. While that is undecided the old ink is drawn faded.
- If the model is still loading when the child writes, the cell waits for it (up to about 3 s) instead of failing.
- DigitCell variants result/carry/given, place-value colours (--pv-* tint plus a top band), statuses idle/active/correct/wrong/hint (gentle wiggle and glow, no red screens), sizes sm/md/lg and bigCells (×1.2). prefers-reduced-motion is honoured everywhere.
- NumberInput: a wide pad sized by maxDigits. Strokes are split into digits by clustering bounding boxes along x: widest strokes go first; a narrow stroke joins a digit if its centre is inside it and it is short or actually touches it (second stroke of a 4); detached hats/bars are merged; tiny dots are dropped. Each digit is re-centred into a single-cell zone before recognition, and the typeset digits are spread so they never overlap.
- NumberInput editing: tapping an unsure digit gives alternatives; tapping a sure one removes it; scribbling erases only the digits underneath; the eraser removes individual strokes. Keyboard digits (capped at maxDigits), Backspace, Enter and Escape work. The big ✓ button and Enter recognise any pending ink before calling onSubmit. In keypad mode or via the 123 toggle, an inline keypad appears and the duplicate eraser/✓ buttons are hidden.
- CellGroup: focus order 'dom' | 'reverse' | 'rtl-columns' (units result, tens carry, tens result, …) or a list of cellIds; roving tabindex; auto-advance after typed digits only (not after handwriting); arrows move spatially; Tab follows the order and leaves the group at the end; Backspace on an empty cell goes back and clears; Enter and the keypad ✓ submit after recognising pending cells. It can show a keypad (below/right/left) and a fallback 123 toggle.
- InkProvider: one shared recogniser loaded once; loads the child's samples (listInkSamples) into setPersonalSamples, passing image28 so samples survive model updates. Learning store: report/confirm/discard plus a counter of recognition fixes. Input mode comes from resolveInputMode; physical-keyboard use on a tablet switches auto mode to 'keyboard'; setPreferred saves through updateChild.
- CalibrationFlow: digits 1–9 then 0, each written twice next to a school model that animates its strokes, with the companion (CompanionArt) and speech bubbles, a progress row, Borrar and Saltar. Samples are stored as 'calibration'. Ink that is too small gets "Hazlo un poco más grande, porfa." The finale reads "¡{pet} ya conoce tu letra!" with celebrate('stars').
- TraceDigit: dotted school model (digitModels.ts, Spanish stroke order with child-facing tips), numbered green start dots, arrows, "Mira" animation, scoring by coverage/precision/start point giving 1–3 stars (starting at the wrong end caps it at 2), result card beside the tracing area, Otra vez / Seguir. Changing the digit starts a fresh exercise.

Visual check: I captured every gallery entry separately on ipad, android and ipad-portrait (calibration) and looked at each. Fixes made after looking: arrow and start-dot design, the 3's shape, keypad-mode layout, trace result moved out of the drawing area, alternatives demo timing.
publicApi:
src/ink/index.ts:
- InkProvider({ children, childId?, recognizer? }) — `recognizer` is an optional injection for tests/gallery.
- useInputMode() → { mode, setPreferred(pref), isTouchDevice, penSeen, preference, forgetPen() } — preference and forgetPen are extra.
- useRecognizer() → { ready, recognize | null }
- DigitCell(DigitCellProps & { cellId?, showClear?, className? }). onChange's second argument is actually an InkChangeInfo { confidence, via, recognitionFix? }.
- NumberInput(NumberInputProps & { ariaLabel?, className?, keypadToggle? })
- Keypad({ onDigit, onDelete, onSubmit?, disabled?, layout?: 'grid' | 'wide', size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg', className?, submitDisabled? })
- CalibrationFlow({ childId, companionName, onDone, repeats? })
- TraceDigit({ digit, onDone(result: { stars: 1 | 2 | 3; score: number }), className? }) — callers passing () => void still work.
- Allowed extras: useInkLearning() → { confirm(), discard(), recognitionFixes() }; CellGroup({ children, order?: 'dom' | 'reverse' | 'rtl-columns' | string[], onSubmit?, autoAdvance?, keypad?: 'auto' | 'show' | 'hide', keypadToggle?, keypadPosition?, keypadLayout?, className?, style? }).
- Type exports: InkChangeInfo, InkVia, CellGroupProps, CellOrder, KeypadProps, InkLearning, InputModeState.
tests:
- npm run typecheck 2>&1 | grep src/ink | grep -v src/ink/ml → 0 lines. Full typecheck: the only errors anywhere are in src/ink/ml (ml agent's testUtils.ts uses node types).
- npx vitest run src/ink --exclude 'src/ink/ml/**' → 11 files, 84 tests, all passed. Files: geometry, policy, order, trace, learning, capture, render, DigitCell, CellGroup, NumberInput, Keypad.
- Running npx vitest run src/ink with ml included shows 3 failures, all in the ml agent's files: two timing assertions under parallel load and one preprocess test.
- npx playwright test tests/e2e/ink.spec.ts → 3 passed, using the real model: keyboard fill/clear; pen-drawn 7, 1, 4, 0 recognised in a DigitCell; pen-written "47" segmented and submitted through ✓. The recognition tests skip with a clear message if public/models/digits/model.json is missing.
- npx oxlint src/ink (excluding ml) → 0 errors; a few remaining warnings are deliberate effect dependencies and gallery helpers.
- Functional Playwright check of CalibrationFlow with the real model: a sample is saved, then "¡Otra vez el 1!", then it moves on to 2.
openIssues: Not mine, but it is what the user asked about: supabase/migrations/ is still empty (0001_init.sql, which docs/SUPABASE_SETUP.md step 3 points to, does not exist) and src/data/index.ts is still a stub. addInkSample / listInkSamples / updateChild therefore do nothing yet, so handwriting samples and the input preference are not saved until the data agent lands.

There is no playwright.config.ts in the repo. The spec uses absolute URLs (E2E_BASE_URL, default http://localhost:5173) and passes with Playwright's defaults; the integrator should add a config (testDir tests/e2e, baseURL, webServer).
The character art is still the integrator's emoji stub, so CalibrationFlow screenshots show an emoji cat; it will pick up the real CompanionArt automatically.
In iPad portrait at 820px the calibration layout wraps (pad below the model); the gallery frame is only 740px tall so it cuts off the footer, but a full-height screen has room.
Synthetic e2e pointer events are not trusted, so they never set penSeen; real-device palm rejection still needs a check on an iPad with Apple Pencil and on an Android tablet with S Pen.
contractRequests: src/types/ink.ts DigitCellProps.onChange info: add `recognitionFix?: boolean`. DigitCell already sends it at runtime (typed as InkChangeInfo) when the child picks a different alternative.

src/types/ink.ts: document the extra hooks in the contract. useInkLearning().recognitionFixes() is how activities fill ExerciseOutcome.recognitionFixes; read it before calling confirm() or discard(), which reset it.

Optional: add `forgetPen()` to the adult settings (e.g. 'Ya no uso lápiz en este dispositivo'). Once a pen has been seen, fingers stop writing until the preference is changed to keypad or forgetPen() is called.
Optional: InkSample could carry `modelId`. The ml recogniser supports it; for now image28 is always stored, so embeddings can be recomputed after a model update.
notesForOtherModules: Activities: wrap a column operation's cells in <CellGroup order="rtl-columns" onSubmit={check}> (or pass an explicit list of cellIds). Give given operands variant="given" and place colours with place="u"|"d"|"c"|"um". Enter and the keypad ✓ call onSubmit only after pending handwriting has been recognised and the parent has re-rendered.
Activities: after a CORRECT answer call useInkLearning().confirm(); after a wrong one call discard(). Read recognitionFixes() first to fill ExerciseOutcome.recognitionFixes.
NumberInput.onSubmit(value) receives the freshly recognised value, so do not read your own state for it. A value of null means nothing readable was written.
DigitCell / NumberInput are controlled components: setting value to null (next exercise) clears the ink; setting a number shows it typeset.

Report inputMode from useInputMode().mode (pen / touch / keyboard / keypad) for fluency thresholds. In 'keypad' mode, NumberInput and CellGroup show an on-screen keypad and a lone DigitCell opens a digit picker on tap.

world-core onboarding: <CalibrationFlow childId companionName onDone /> fills its container (min-height 100%), so put it inside your Screen. It reads the companion art from useActiveChild(). Set your 'calibration' progress flag in onDone.
TraceDigit is meant for digits a child often has misread (e.g. high recognitionFixes for 4 or 7); its onDone receives { stars, score }.

Gallery: /dev/gallery?only=src/ink/ink.gallery. The 'Prueba con el modelo real' entries use the app's real recogniser (used by the e2e test); the other demos replay synthetic pen strokes through a scripted recogniser.
metrics: Real-model e2e: synthetic pen-drawn 7, 1, 4, 0 recognised in a DigitCell, and "47" in the NumberInput. Segmentation unit tests pass for 42, 57, 74, 100, 11, 648 and 9, for strokes written out of order, slightly overlapping digits, a detached 5 hat and noise dots. The scribble detector never fires on any digit 0–9 (including a 0 traced twice). Tracing gives 3 stars for careful traces of all 10 digits and 1 star for the wrong digit. Recognition fires 620 ms after pen-up; a stroke within 1.8 s continues the same digit.
